shape selectivity in V4 and motion selectivity in MT are different in the time domain, and that these temporal differences are likely to reflect the interaction between V4 and MT.
shape and motion processing in the primate brain is not completely segregated but rather is integrated at a later stage in the ventral visual cortical areas.
visual response latencies of shape-selective V4 neurons were longer in the motion-cued condition than in the luminance cued condition.

the temporal properties of neuronal activity in response to shape stimuli in different visual cortical areas.
the visual processing of the shape defined by the motion and luminance cue.
the neural basis of shape perception and the interaction of shape perception and motion perception.

shape selectivity is initiated in both V4 and the anterior superior sulcus in a similar timing, but that the shape selectivity is more pronounced and sustained in the anterior superior sulcusanterior middle temporal sulcus region than in V4.
shape perception is not achieved in a single cortical area but rather in a distributed network of cortical areas.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shape perception with motion cues requires a longer processing time than shape perception with luminance cues.
the temporal property of neural activities in V4 and MT is different in the motion-cued condition compared to the luminance-cued condition.
the ventral cortex is involved in motion-defined shape perception, and the timing of initiation of shape modulation in the ventral cortex differs between motion- and luminance-defined conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual system is able to process motion-defined shape perception through an interaction between ventral and motion areas.
shape selectivity in V4 and the middle temporal area is different depending on the visual cues used to define the shape.
motion and shape are not processed exclusively in the dorsal or ventral cortical areas but that the ventral and the dorsal areas interact in the process of motion-defined shape perception.
